one_liner: A court reporter who takes down House floor debates, hearings and markups word-for-word at high speed and produces edited official transcripts.
fit_summary: This skilled stenography job requires extensive experience reporting multi-voice hearings at very high speeds, and NCRA or state certification is strongly preferred. Daniel's resume has no court-reporting or machine-shorthand training (his meeting minutes are a different skill), so skip it.
eligibility: Open to the public (hiring path: public), so no prior federal status is needed.
Requires extensive knowledge and experience in reporting, plus the ability to report multi-voice hearings at very high speeds.
An NCRA proficiency certification or a similar state certification is strongly preferred.
A Top Secret national security clearance is required, and this is a Test Designated Position subject to random drug testing.
This is a House (legislative branch) HS-12 position, so executive-branch time-in-grade rules do not apply.
keywords: Rules and procedures of the House
strategy: Skip this one: it requires stenographic or voice-writing skills at professional speed, and his meeting minutes are a different skill.
Look instead at House or Senate staff roles such as staff assistant or legislative correspondent, which suit his close interest in politics and policy.
resume_bullets: Took minutes at a large travel company's weekly meetings (Feb – Aug 2024) and at a state public health agency's mpox response meetings (Dec 2022 – Mar 2023).
Delivered detailed notes used to write after-action reports for FEMA full-scale exercises.
interview_questions: What certification and realtime speed do you hold, and how do you handle multi-voice crosstalk in a hearing?
How would you reflect a motion to recommit or a unanimous consent request accurately in a transcript?
Describe a time you met a tight deadline after a long day while keeping accuracy high.
How do you protect classified or confidential material in your work?
watch_outs: The core requirement is high-speed verbatim reporting, a specialized skill his resume doesn't show.
A Top Secret clearance and random drug testing are required.
The role requires long hours, nights, and weekends, with no telework, plus a commute from Manassas to the Capitol.
NCRA or state certification is strongly preferred, and acquiring one takes years of training.
